system.biography:
Jules "Patch" Akin — Dead Air Collective coordinator (Dead Air Collective, patron). Fictional.

At DA2 Cafe OTO (Dalston): Dead Air coordinator. An invented experimental performance contains the genuine source of a sound later reused in the warning; the session owner has a rival offer.

At DA7 Backspin Studio (Dalston). The fictional pirate station's core studio can become independent, sponsored or controlled by a faction.

At ST4 Theatre Royal Stratford East (Stratford & the Stadium): visiting coordinator. An invented theatre benefit puts a missing performer's belongings and an employer's ultimatum backstage just before the curtain rises.

At BF5 UCL East Marshgate (Bow Flyover & Mill Meads): visiting coordinator. An invented public showcase gives a survey witness a place to compare a model with the earlier genuine plan and the later contractor's version.

Gives: AD1, AD2, AD3, AD5, AD6, AD8.

Dee Hassan — station technician (Dead Air Collective). Fictional.

Dee Hassan wants practical independence;

At DA4 Vortex Jazz Club (Dalston). A fictional late set carries an unscheduled dedication from a missing contact, and the person offering the recording cannot explain its date.

At ST8 Bridge Nine Broadcast Garage (Stratford & the Stadium). A fictional mobile station base lets the crew choose who gets the final live slot and who pays for it.

Gives: AD4.

Leon Marsh — retired sound engineer and archivist (Dead Air Collective). Fictional.

Leon Marsh wants the archive respected;

At HB2 The Old Church (Highbury & Albion Rd): retired sound engineer. A small late-night performance uses an old station ident that should not exist on the apparent new warning; an uncredited performer wants their fee before helping.

At LF8 Englefield Listening Flat (Haggerston & London Fields). Private station recordings can be authenticated here, while a rival waits outside with a much better cash offer.

Gives: AD7.

Nia "Switch" Bell — radio presenter (Dead Air Collective). Fictional.

Nia Switch Bell wants control over her own account.

At BF6 Pudding Mill Lane DLR station (Bow Flyover & Mill Meads): radio presenter by arrangement. A fictional passenger's handover is interrupted by the arriving train, splitting the crew's attention between a stolen case and the person holding its receipt.

Victor "Vic" Randle — bookmaker and lender (The Backroom Bookmakers, patron). Fictional.

At LY3 The Leyton Engineer (Leyton & Ruckholt): bookmaker. A bookmaker's agent offers a lucrative early result while a previous winner arrives to collect money that was never set aside.

At LY7 Third Half Bookroom (Leyton & Ruckholt). Vic's real debts and an invented collection racket share a ledger he wants back before his staff read it.

Gives: BB1, BB2, BB3, BB4, BB5, BB6, BB7.

Eddie Lane — bookmaker's cashier (The Backroom Bookmakers). Fictional.

Cashier Eddie Lane wants genuine debts separated from invented ones;

At WS8 Well Street Loan Office (South Hackney & Well Street). A profitable collection business is charging genuine accounts twice and a clerk wants a share to keep quiet.

At HX3 Rosemary Branch Theatre (Hoxton West & the Canal). An invented performance has a missing prop chest whose contents connect an ordinary worker to a valuable old object.

Frankie Wu — accountant (The Backroom Bookmakers). Fictional.

accountant Frankie Wu wants records that will survive scrutiny.

At DB6 The Talbot (De Beauvoir). A fictional promoter offers a private fee to alter a programme, while the performer affected by it waits at another table.

At HX6 The Baring (Hoxton West & the Canal). A fictional investor meal exposes who actually guaranteed a transport contract, and a private consultancy offer tests the crew's existing promises.

At HX8 Shepherdess Coin Rooms (Hoxton West & the Canal). Two lenders have sold the same debt and each has hired a different crew to enforce it.

Rosa Baptiste — mutual-aid organiser (Borough Mutual, patron). Fictional.

At SN1 Abney Park Chapel (Stoke Newington & Shacklewell). A memorial recording contains a living person's interruption; a private event gives the crew a deadline before the reel is sold.

At SN7 Saint Martha House (Stoke Newington & Shacklewell). A proposed faction base with competing demands on the same room, money and volunteers.

At WS5 St John of Jerusalem (South Hackney & Well Street): visiting organiser. An invented advice meeting holds an original petition that can expose a false redevelopment mandate before the courier returns for it.

Gives: BM1, BM2, BM3, BM4, BM5, BM6, BM7, BM8.

Adele Mensah — tenant representative (Borough Mutual). Fictional.

Tenant Adele Mensah wants concrete guarantees;

At CL5 Clapton Country Club (Clapton). An invented auction or benefit books performers, lenders and property buyers into one crowded building with one crucial service case.

At CL8 Clapton Union Rooms (Clapton). One of the six targeted premises; an early acquisition list names the building while its workshops are still occupied.

Gwen Price — tenant organiser (Borough Mutual). Fictional.

organiser Gwen Price wants a funded future.

At BF2 The View Tube (Bow Flyover & Mill Meads). A fictional courier meeting at the cafe identifies four loads with one payer; a rival's van is due before the runner finishes their break.

At BF8 Carpenters Breakfast Club (Bow Flyover & Mill Meads). One of the six targeted premises; a redevelopment mandate was assembled from an ordinary repair petition.

Tariq Evans — patient advocate (Borough Mutual). Fictional.

advocate Tariq Evans protects individual consent;

At HC3 Sutton House (Hackney Central & Homerton). An invented private-view loan links a family photograph to an intermediary's older identity; a collector tries to buy the supporting papers separately.

At BG8 Approach Recovery Rooms (Bethnal Green). An invented support venue holds willing witnesses and relatives with different demands on the crew's protection.

Auntie Pat — Chainring fence and fixer (The Chainring, patron). Fictional.

Pat prefers discretion, Spanner wants more legitimate work, and Sal's ambition can attract members who want a more forceful operation.

At HC1 Hackney Empire (Hackney Central & Homerton): established fixer. An invented benefit concert has a stolen backstage case, unpaid performers and an intermediary who needs one particular speaker kept off the bill.

Gives: CH4, CH5, CH6, CH7, CH8.

Big Sal — Chainring muscle (The Chainring). Fictional.

Pat prefers discretion, Spanner wants more legitimate work, and Sal's ambition can attract members who want a more forceful operation.

Gives: S13.

Kez — Chainring runner (The Chainring). Fictional.

Kez wants people treated as friends rather than expendable runners.

At HC8 Clifden Crew Garage (Hackney Central & Homerton). A possible crew property starts with an unresolved tenancy and an engine nobody admits owning.

At LF3 The Duke of Richmond (Haggerston & London Fields): established runner. A fictional collector holds a bicycle inspection here while a runner asks the crew to distract the buyer long enough to retrieve a personal object.

At WS4 The Lauriston (South Hackney & Well Street): established tip-off contact. A fictional promoter and a tenant organiser discover their benefits were pledged the same equipment; the supplier's receipt points to a third patron.

At HR1 Museum of the Home (Haggerston Park & Hackney Rd): established rider. An invented oral-history evening contains an older account of Quayline's intermediary under a different professional name.

Gives: S17.

Spanner Rob — Chainring mechanic (The Chainring). Fictional.

Spanner Rob wants a sustainable workshop;

At HC7 Chainring Storehouse (Hackney Central & Homerton). Pat can grant a working base here; a rival claims the building and cargo as separate debts.

At LF1 London Fields Lido (Haggerston & London Fields): visiting mechanic. An invented cycling fundraiser draws thieves to the racks and a runner to the foyer; the same place can support a score, a chase and a later legitimate event.

Clement Wren — art broker (The Glasshouse Exchange, patron). Fictional.

Wren thinks he can preserve both until a major property sale makes neutrality expensive.

At CG2 Estorick Collection (Canonbury & Newington Green). An invented loan exhibition is missing its final crate; the crew must separate the artist's object from the papers someone concealed inside it.

At CG7 Glasshouse Saleroom (Canonbury & Newington Green). An invitation-only fictional auction offers stolen objects and private property options in the same catalogue.

At OF1 St Mary Bow Church (Old Ford & Bow): visiting broker. An invented quiet meeting connects a frightened witness with a possible supporter while a rival tries to buy the meeting's location.

Gives: GE1, GE3, GE4, GE5, GE6, GE8, S06.

Evie Slate — fixer (The Glasshouse Exchange). Fictional.

fixer Evie Slate prefers profitable uncertainty.

Iris Bellamy — curator and collection assistant (The Glasshouse Exchange). Fictional.

curator Iris Bellamy wants honest loans;

At BG5 Bethnal Green Library (Bethnal Green): collection assistant. A local-history enquiry identifies a missing witness through public material and an old workshop address, without relying on an invented institutional conspiracy.

Luca Ferretti — restorer (The Glasshouse Exchange). Fictional.

Restorer Luca Ferretti cares about ownership;

At DB2 De Beauvoir Deli (De Beauvoir). A fictional courier's ordinary food delivery contains a private envelope intended for a different household; its buyer is already on the way.

Oona Reyes — performer and costume artist (The Glasshouse Exchange). Fictional.

Gives: GE2.

Stretch — Lea Boys leader (The Lea Boys, patron). Fictional.

Stretch favours a Meridian partnership.

Daz Riley — Lea Boys collector (The Lea Boys). Fictional.

collector Daz Riley wants quick money and status.

Tessa "Moth" Price — Lea Boys organiser (The Lea Boys). Fictional.

Tessa Moth Price values territorial loyalty;

At CL3 The Crooked Billet (Clapton). A fictional collector counts protection money in the snug while Moth's rival wants the crew to catch him keeping part of it.

At CL7 Lea Bridge Social Rooms (Clapton). Stretch's collectors and Moth's supporters hold incompatible versions of the same debt book.

Gives: LB1, LB2, LB3, LB4, LB5, LB6, LB7.

DS Harriet Vale — detective sergeant (The Lantern Desk, patron). Fictional.

Vale's caution competes with her ambition.

At BG2 The Approach Tavern and Gallery (Bethnal Green): established detective. A fictional visiting artist's upper-gallery preview puts a stolen crate within reach of a fence who has promised it to another patron.

At BG7 Lantern Case Flat (Bethnal Green). Vale's fictional source meeting place is a relationship with a detective, not a police station the crew can command.

Gives: LD1, LD2, LD3, LD4, LD5, LD6, LD7, LD8.

Inspector Gavin Holt — police inspector (The Lantern Desk). Fictional.

Inspector Gavin Holt wants inconvenient accounts contained. Holt has taken consultancy money and helped suppress accounts, but cannot control every officer or every record.

PC Isla Dunn — frustrated police officer (The Lantern Desk). Fictional.

PC Isla Dunn wants her original note heard; Dunn fears becoming a scapegoat.

At SN4 The Red Lion (Stoke Newington & Shacklewell): frustrated officer. A backroom card-night contact offers an introduction in exchange for recovering their genuine property from a dishonest collector.

Celia Voss — Meridian Renewal director (Meridian Renewal, patron). Fictional.

At ON2 Lee Valley Hockey and Tennis Centre (Olympic Park North): Meridian director. A fictional sporting fundraiser loses a prize case while its organiser tries to avoid admitting that the prize was borrowed.

At ON8 North Park Hospitality Lodge (Olympic Park North). The fictional investor reception offers the crew money, a future role and several incompatible promises.

At ST2 London Stadium (Stratford & the Stadium): developer. An invented concert in a fictional visitor wing brings final-night publicity and a disputed load to the stadium without involving the real teams or operator in the scheme.

At ST7 Meridian Sales Pavilion (Stratford & the Stadium). The final signatures happen here, but transport, testimony and the public programme have separate control points.

Gives: MR2, MR4, MR5, MR6, MR8.

Esther Cole — survey technician (Meridian Renewal). Fictional.

surveyor Esther Cole wants truthful work;

At CG6 Highbury Leisure Centre (Canonbury & Newington Green). An invented training event provides cover for a private meeting between a runner and a lender, while the runner's actual sponsor waits outside.

Evan Lark — Meridian intermediary (Meridian Renewal). Fictional.

intermediary Evan Lark handles the unattractive details.

At CG8 Quayline Records Suite (Canonbury & Newington Green). Lark's consultancy coordinates the acquisition payments without containing a convenient single confession.

Martin Rusk — Meridian security chief (Meridian Renewal). Fictional.

Security chief Martin Rusk wants control; Rusk has escalated intimidation and paid for deception.

At WW5 The Kenton (Homerton East & Wick Woodland). A fictional benefit organiser has paid for a projector that is being collected by a rival event; the crew can recover it or sell the booking twice.

At WW8 East Cross Security Compound (Homerton East & Wick Woodland). Rusk's fictional contractor has staff schedules and vehicles that place coercion before the supposed emergency.

Gives: MR1, MR3, MR7.

Pearl Okonkwo — trader coordinator (The Night Market, patron). Fictional.

At CL2 The Princess of Wales (Clapton). A courier's boat-side meeting is interrupted by two buyers claiming the same sealed load; the pub is neutral ground until one starts a fight.

At DA1 Rio Cinema (Dalston): visiting trader. A fictional station film night includes a threatening message on a reel delivered by the wrong courier; the projection deadline forces a choice.

At BG3 York Hall (Bethnal Green). A fictional adult prizefight uses Sal's photograph without agreement; a genuine promoter has spent the advance and a rival wants the show cancelled.

At OF3 The Lord Morpeth (Old Ford & Bow): visiting coordinator. A fictional bookmaker's collector arrives during a market worker's break to demand cash already paid to someone using the same name.

Gives: NM1, NM2, NM3, NM4, NM5, NM6, NM7, NM8, S19.

Len Fisk — resale broker (The Night Market). Fictional.

broker Len Fisk wants an exclusive resale concession.

Nessa Grey — clothes trader (The Night Market). Fictional.

Trader Nessa Grey protects her customers;

At DA5 EartH (Dalston). An invented festival loses its principal hire fee; a promoter is trying to move an unrelated private consignment among the returning cases.

Ada "Index" March — Red Thread researcher (The Red Thread, patron). Fictional.

At DB1 St Peter de Beauvoir (De Beauvoir). An invented evening meeting brings a missing person's family into contact with someone who knows they left voluntarily.

At DB7 Split Second Archive (De Beauvoir). An independent investigation network needs originals preserved and a decision about who may sell the story.

At ST6 V&A East Museum (Stratford & the Stadium): visiting researcher. An invented public-history event can preserve a narrow supported account or sell a much broader story; the visiting campaign parties disagree about what it proves.

Gives: RT1, RT2, RT3, RT4, RT5, RT6, RT7, RT8.

Noel Harris — local-history volunteer (The Red Thread). Fictional.

Noel Harris values oral history;

At HR6 Sebright Arms (Haggerston Park & Hackney Rd). A fictional newcomer is offered a first broadcast slot at the price of endorsing an accusation they cannot verify.

Zoe Akande — community solicitor (The Red Thread). Fictional.

solicitor Zoe Akande insists on clear agreements;

At CG4 Union Chapel (Canonbury & Newington Green). A fictional benefit performance needs one disputed sound case and a performer who will not accept another empty promise of later payment.

Mara "Tern" Boyd — Towpath Union dispatcher (The Towpath Union, patron). Fictional.

At HX2 The Eagle (Hoxton West & the Canal). A fictional promoter has promised the same private meeting to two factions and borrowed a third party's cash to pay for it.

At HX7 Tern Wharf Dispatch (Hoxton West & the Canal). The network's contracts, vehicles and workers can be split between a cooperative, a criminal patron and Meridian.

At BF1 ABBA Arena (Bow Flyover & Mill Meads): visiting dispatcher. An invented off-night production hire brings a missing equipment case and a false guest list into a fictional event wing, separate from the actual show.

Gives: TU1, TU2, TU3, TU4, TU5, TU6, TU7, TU8, S14, S20.

Gita Mercer — dispatcher and stores keeper (The Towpath Union). Fictional.

Dispatcher Gita Mercer protects workers;

At HX1 The Wenlock Arms (Hoxton West & the Canal): stores keeper. A fictional repair contact has a tape case with a new owner and an old hidden repair ticket that dates the original session.

At BF7 Marshgate Delivery Depot (Bow Flyover & Mill Meads). Four final-night loads have the same customer, but one is routine business and another moves a witness's belongings.

Yasmin Dale — driver and fleet coordinator (The Towpath Union). Fictional.

driver Yasmin Dale wants contracts that cannot discard her staff overnight.

At DB3 De Beauvoir Block (De Beauvoir): fleet coordinator. A fictional tenant's hired meeting suite has a false consultancy invoice, a rival bid and a copy the paying patron did not know existed.

At LF7 Kingsland Courier Arch (Haggerston & London Fields). A vanished parcel is less important than the witness who signed for it under someone else's name.

Owen Pike — promoter and nightlife bookkeeper (The Velvet Circuit, patron). Fictional.

At DA3 Dalston Superstore (Dalston): nightlife bookkeeper. A fictional visiting promoter offers an exclusive slot to buy a missing performer's silence; the performer has brought an ally and a competing plan.

At DA8 Blue Hour Basement (Dalston). A fictional club beneath invented premises links promoter money, Halo stock and an attempted cover-up.

At BF3 The House Mill (Bow Flyover & Mill Meads): visiting bookkeeper. An invented heritage fundraiser has a returned ledger, a substituted donation and a witness who knows where an independent thief sold the original.

Gives: VC1, VC2, VC3, VC4, VC5, VC6.

Mara Sol — performer (The Velvet Circuit). Fictional.

performer Mara Sol wants a future without Owen's control.

Reece Hale — door manager (The Velvet Circuit). Fictional.

Door manager Reece Hale wants staff paid;

At ST3 London Aquatics Centre (Stratford & the Stadium): event supervisor. A fictional sporting event offers a witness meeting, a valuable prize and a delivery the dispatcher has misidentified.

Ada Finch — sound artist. Fictional.

At WW3 The Adam and Eve (Homerton East & Wick Woodland). A fictional hire driver is waiting for their next job when two collectors arrive for different vans of the same colour.

Alix Porter — event stores keeper. Fictional.

At VW6 People's Park Tavern (Victoria Park & Hackney Wick). A fictional sponsor has bought a benefit's publicity without paying the workers; a public performance creates a deadline for an honest or profitable settlement.

Amina Keane — equipment-hire owner. Fictional.

At HR4 Haggerston Community Centre (Haggerston Park & Hackney Rd). An invented crew meeting can become a funded youth riding project, a recruitment front or the scene of a rival's accusation; the campaign participants are fictional.

At HR7 Queensbridge Sound Store (Haggerston Park & Hackney Rd). One missing sound system is pledged to two events; an unpaid crew has moved it for a third client.

Amir Costa — amateur match organiser. Fictional.

At HM5 Temple Mills International Depot (Hackney Marshes). A fictional interview and collection at an invented visitor wing identifies a witness by work history; the railway operation itself is not the criminal organisation.

Anya Byrne — stage manager. Fictional.

At HC4 Oslo Hackney (Hackney Central & Homerton). A fictional hire collection collides with another gig's load-out, creating a moving van encounter before the crew knows which case is theirs.

Arthur Venn — retired cabbie. Fictional.

Gives: S18.

Asha Stone — retired care worker. Fictional.

At WW4 The Spread Eagle (Homerton East & Wick Woodland). A fictional courier left a bag under the wrong table; one customer wants the ordinary contents back while another wants the envelope hidden inside.

At WW7 Willow Cabin (Homerton East & Wick Woodland). Nia Switch Bell is alive here at the start; her evidence and her present whereabouts are separate bargaining issues.

Basil Armitage — cab dispatcher. Fictional.

At CL6 The Elderfield (Clapton). A fictional match fixer meets a runner here; the crew can steal the payoff, expose the offer or buy the runner a different exit.

At HC5 MOTH Club (Hackney Central & Homerton): visiting dispatcher. An invented club meeting is carrying a faction leadership vote under cover of an ordinary social night; a rival brings a creditor as leverage.

Beatrice Shaw — executor. Fictional.

At CG3 The Canonbury Tavern (Canonbury & Newington Green). A collector holds a private preview upstairs, where a familiar frame has a new ownership story and a much higher price.

Carmen Sloane — night manager. Fictional.

At ST5 Sadler's Wells East (Stratford & the Stadium). An invented late performance gives the crew an alternate stage for an appeal when the main station programme is bought or interrupted.

Daniel Firth — committee clerk. Fictional.

At WS3 The Gun (South Hackney & Well Street). A fictional collector uses an ordinary pub meeting to sell a protection claim they do not own, with a second crew waiting for the same fee.

Darren "Tabs" Ellis — club secretary. Fictional.

At SN6 St Paul's West Hackney (Stoke Newington & Shacklewell). An invented tenant meeting holds the clean copy of a repair petition; someone wants it replaced before the public account becomes fixed.

At SN8 Evering Safe Flat (Stoke Newington & Shacklewell). A collector has paid for a refuge but believes that makes its guest his property.

Della Finch — cycle collector. Fictional.

At HB1 Clissold House (Highbury & Albion Rd). A fictional donor's reception conceals a missing envelope among coats and catering cases; the crew can steal it, buy it or expose its owner at the wrong moment.

Dennis Crowe — repairer. Fictional.

At HX5 The Narrowboat (Hoxton West & the Canal). A fictional canal courier waits for a buyer while a second crew approaches from the towpath, turning a quiet sale into a pursuit or three-way bargain.

Eileen Grant — residents' organiser. Fictional.

At VW4 Grow Hackney (Victoria Park & Hackney Wick). An invented arts night includes an audio installation whose background sound disproves the claimed location of the warning.

At VW8 White Post Workers Rooms (Victoria Park & Hackney Wick). One of the six targeted premises; residents and workers disagree about a relocation offer made under a false account.

Ellis Morgan — event organiser. Fictional.

At HC6 The Castle Cinema (Hackney Central & Homerton). A fictional screening contains an accidental glimpse of a disputed van handover; the camera's owner wants to sell the full version before the show.

Ewan Cole — garage proprietor. Fictional.

At ON3 Timber Lodge (Olympic Park North). A fictional race checkpoint receives the result before the runners arrive, giving the crew a narrow chance to catch the person selling it.

Ezra Holt — youth rowing volunteer. Fictional.

At CL4 The Clapton Hart (Clapton). A missing-person appeal brings a genuine old friend and a paid false witness to the same table.

Farah Yilmaz — hall steward. Fictional.

At HB6 The Rose and Crown (Highbury & Albion Rd). A guest at an invented private function has pledged the same tape as security to two lenders, both of whom have sent collectors.

Felix Dyer — café employee. Fictional.

At LF4 The Spurstowe Arms (Haggerston & London Fields). A fictional buyer for the Whippet changes the meeting into an argument over the promised model, its ownership and the agreed price.

Giles Archer — pawnbroker. Fictional.

At LY5 Score Leisure Centre (Leyton & Ruckholt). A fictional runner's sponsor has promised two athletes the same exclusive; a changing-room confrontation becomes a public race-time choice.

Grace Okafor — tenant and warehouse keeper. Fictional.

At DB4 The De Beauvoir Arms (De Beauvoir). A fictional letting clerk meets workers over a pint and realises their premises were described as vacant before the proposed inspection.

At DB8 Essex Dry Goods (De Beauvoir). One of the six targeted premises; the workers are present despite a prewritten inventory describing it as empty.

Gwen Hollis — canal volunteer. Fictional.

At HM6 Leyton Jubilee Park pavilion (Hackney Marshes). A fictional sports booking has been sold twice, leaving an event fee, a vanished organiser and a genuine crowd waiting for doors to open.

Hassan Arif — parts dealer. Fictional.

At LY2 Leyton Orient Supporters Club (Leyton & Ruckholt). A fictional supporters' fundraiser loses its takings; the treasurer's honest mistake gives a separate thief cover to move the envelope.

Helen Drew — event administrator. Fictional.

At ON6 The Leyton Star (Olympic Park North). A fictional lender pays for a runner's kit and later calls it a debt; a private settlement can become a theft, a public row or a new sponsorship.

Imogen Vale — record seller. Fictional.

At SN2 Abney Books (Stoke Newington & Shacklewell). A donation includes a betting book hidden inside a family history; its donor wants one page returned before anyone reads the rest.

Indira Shaw — workshop manager. Fictional.

At VW1 Barge East (Victoria Park & Hackney Wick). A fictional private dining meeting takes place aboard the barge while a courier waits dockside with a case that belongs to neither diner.

Ivo Marsh — parcel clerk. Fictional.

At OF6 Forman's Fish Island (Old Ford & Bow). An invented private reception puts a contractor and a lender at adjacent tables while a visiting courier is offered money to change their account.

Jonah Mills — book club secretary. Fictional.

Gives: S01.

Jonah Reed — bookseller. Fictional.

At HB5 Stoke Newington Town Hall (Highbury & Albion Rd). A fictional property hearing puts the crew, tenant representatives and a paid intermediary in one room with a short speaking slot and a missing original.

Juno Peters — centre caretaker. Fictional.

At WW1 Hackney Marshes Centre (Homerton East & Wick Woodland). A fictional recovery job moves through the sports complex while a charity delivery and a valuable bike shipment arrive together.

Kenji Ward — night-shift porter. Fictional.

At HM3 New Spitalfields Market administration (Hackney Marshes). A fictional hire enquiry uncovers two invoices issued for the same journey and an original that a courier will collect at closing.

Kit Dey — print worker. Fictional.

At OF4 St Paul Old Ford (Old Ford & Bow). An invented residents' meeting has two genuine relocation proposals and an unsigned petition that an intermediary wants to claim as universal support.

At OF8 Roman Rooms Printworks (Old Ford & Bow). One of the six targeted premises; a clearance leaflet was produced before the incident it claims to summarise.

Leila Trent — bar manager. Fictional.

At HX4 Victoria Miro (Hoxton West & the Canal). An invented loan viewing attracts a collector, a restorer and an artist with incompatible rights to the same crate.

Dr Lena Morris — volunteer clinician. Fictional.

At BG4 St John on Bethnal Green (Bethnal Green). An invented memorial appeal is collecting money for a living cab driver; the embarrassed family and the dishonest broker need different resolutions.

Lenora Pike — tenants' secretary. Fictional.

At WS2 Hackney Picturehouse (South Hackney & Well Street). An invented film event puts a private witness account on the programme without the speaker's agreement; the full recording also clears a driver.

Liv Barrett — freight clerk. Fictional.

At LY6 The Coach and Horses (Leyton & Ruckholt). A private debt settlement puts two authentic claimants beside a forged account; the person carrying the cash plans to leave before anyone compares them.

Mags Cole — off-duty crew representative. Fictional.

At SN5 The Shacklewell Arms (Stoke Newington & Shacklewell). A fictional band's missing sound case is already on a departing van while a promoter announces an expensive replacement hire.

Malcolm "Mal" Reed — retired DJ. Fictional.

At VW2 CRATE Brewery (Victoria Park & Hackney Wick). A fictional event crew has mixed a valuable recording into its hire returns; a rival wants to buy the whole consignment before it is sorted.

Marisol Vega — depot forewoman. Fictional.

At HM2 New Spitalfields Market produce hall (Hackney Marshes). An invented trader's load is being removed during the rush; the crew must choose whether to recover a stolen object, follow a person or finish a paid collection.

At HM7 Orient Night Shed (Hackney Marshes). A stolen load is mixed with an ordinary market consignment and two crews expect collection.

Marnie Lowe — venue porter. Fictional.

At LF5 The Duke of Wellington (Haggerston & London Fields). A fictional sound-case exchange is interrupted by a bookmaker's collector who believes its contents settle a different debt.

Marta Severin — warehouse night manager. Fictional.

At LY4 Leyton Great Hall (Leyton & Ruckholt). An invented private gala gives the crew access to a property-options handover, a rival buyer and an upstairs negotiation that can change the price.

At LY8 Larch Cold Store (Leyton & Ruckholt). The fictional Halo shipment changed here; the remaining stock is valuable, harmful and claimed by several patrons.

Maya Foster — personal shopper. Fictional.

At ST1 Westfield Stratford City (Stratford & the Stadium). A fictional collector's private shopping appointment is cover for a stolen-object handover; the crew can follow the object or the person who paid for it.

Mick Okoro — van-hire manager. Fictional.

At VW5 Number 90 (Victoria Park & Hackney Wick). An invented club event has two rival rights to the same headline set and one visitor offering a private fee to stop it happening.

Milo Trent — chef and tenant. Fictional.

At DA6 Dalston CLR James Library (Dalston). A public-history enquiry finds an old credit, a false name and a surviving caller's route into the missing-DJ case.

Mina Dey — pressured letting clerk. Fictional.

At HB4 The Highbury Barn Tavern (Highbury & Albion Rd). A cycle collector meets a fence over a drink while the bicycle's actual owner arrives for the same appointment.

At HB8 Orchard Lease Office (Highbury & Albion Rd). One of the six targeted premises; the tenants' earlier offer survives beside a later false vacancy report.

Mo Rahman — landlord of Chicken Palace. Fictional.

At HC2 Round Chapel (Hackney Central & Homerton): established landlord. A fictional listening night becomes a three-way contest for the microphone, the missing recording and the cash collected at the door.

Gives: S08.

Nadia Sayeed — kiosk owner. Fictional.

At CL1 Clapton Library (Clapton). A local-history enquiry identifies a previous owner of the missing watch and puts the crew on a trail independent of Meridian.

Nell Grant — volunteer steward. Fictional.

At OF5 The Trampery Fish Island Village (Old Ford & Bow). A fictional maker's hired workspace contains the crate that a respectable buyer says was never delivered; its ordinary creator needs their tools returned.

Nico "Blank" Evans — young adult DJ. Fictional.

At HR2 Hoxton Hall (Haggerston Park & Hackney Rd). A fictional benefit performance needs an honest final bill while a sponsor threatens to withdraw the fee already promised to its workers.

Nico Petrescu — contract mechanic. Fictional.

At ON1 Lee Valley VeloPark (Olympic Park North). An invented amateur cycling event brings a valuable frame, a disputed sponsor and two collectors into the visitor and workshop areas.

Noreen Aziz — launderette proprietor. Fictional.

At WS1 Hackney Town Hall (South Hackney & Well Street). A fictional public-gallery session offers a short chance to present genuine papers before an intermediary's misleading account is accepted by the room.

Ollie Grant — grounds caretaker. Fictional.

At HM1 Hackney Marshes North Pavilion (Hackney Marshes). A fictional amateur club's match envelope disappears between the changing corridor and the clubroom; three teams have different reasons to keep quiet.

Oona Dale — costume maker. Fictional.

At HR5 Hackney City Farm (Haggerston Park & Hackney Rd). A fictional adult volunteer's misplaced work bag contains a meeting note sought by a collector; ordinary visitors and the farm's real work remain separate.

Otis Mensah — dispatcher. Fictional.
